newsitem.title: SPAIN: New uses offer potential for copper offtake - IWCC.
newsitem.headline: New uses offer potential for copper offtake - IWCC.

text.p: Copper consumption growth patterns vary globally between developed countries and developing regions, with some potential in both new and existing areas for increased usage, Simon Payton, secretary-general of the International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC), said on Tuesday.
In Asia, with the exception of Japan, consumption prospects were good, but the picture in other areas was mixed at present for copper usage.

"In general I remain optimistic about copper's consumption prospects ... Value growth will come from product innovation and niche marketing," Payton said at Metal Bulletin's International Copper Conference.
In the telecommunications sector densely-populated Asia, for example, lags far behind some European areas in telephone usage.
"75 percent of the world's population have 12 percent of its telephone lines, so there is scope there," Payton said.
In motor vehicles, optional items that were previously confined to luxury top-of-the-range items were filtering down to standard models.
Electric windows, security systems, heaters and air conditioning all needed small electronic motors containing copper to operate.
"Moreover, we have not really started to see the impact of navigation and traffic guidance systems yet, the latter needing the roads to be wired up for sensors," Payton said.
In construction it was not only new building projects where copper was used. There were also possibilities in renovations and improvements.

However, in plumbing plastic substitutes provided a threat, and copper would need to take another approach. Typically, at the end of the pipe there would be a tap often made from a brass casting and using brass components.
In some houses there were some four or five taps, but in densely populated parts of the world one tap served tens or even hundreds of people.
"One tap may contain around one pound of copper. If the world had one per head that is 2.5 million tonnes of copper," Payton said.
There was also the possibility that European Monetary Union would impact on copper usage via a new currency and new coins. In the U.K. there were currently 40,000 tonnes of copper in coins.
Looking at the overall consumption growth picture, Payton said Asian growth would be good bar Japan where copper offtake would grow by just one percent.
U.S. growth would be modest, but Canadian prospects were improving. In Europe, growth rates were also modest, but in eastern Europe the picture was brighter, he added.
